questions.stem: According to the reading text, before any examination begins a patient needs to know:
options: How long you have been working
questions.explanation: "A patient needs to know two things: who you are, and what your role is."

questions.stem: A short, confident introduction, according to the text, includes:
options: A brief explanation of what will happen next
A detailed description of your training
questions.explanation: Name, role and a brief explanation of what will happen next help the patient feel safe.

questions.stem: Why should students and trainees state their role clearly?
options: So the patient does not assume they are a fully qualified doctor or nurse
Because students are not allowed to talk to patients
To avoid confirming the patient's identity
questions.explanation: Students should say so clearly "rather than letting the patient assume they are a fully qualified doctor or nurse".

questions.stem: Confirming the patient's full name and date of birth is described as:
options: A basic safety check before any procedure
questions.explanation: "It is not just politeness; it is also a basic safety check before any procedure."

questions.stem: Which sentences are appropriate for a first-year student meeting a patient?
options: I'm a first-year student; I'll be observing today, if that's alright with you.
I'm the consultant in charge of your case.
questions.explanation: C would let the patient believe the student is a qualified senior doctor.

questions.stem: Which are role nouns listed in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Role nouns: physician, nurse, student nurse, consultant, receptionist, paramedic.

questions.stem: In the model dialogue, what does the nurse do before checking the blood pressure?
options: Asks the patient to confirm his full name and date of birth
Asks for the patient's insurance card
questions.explanation: "My name is Nadia, and I'll be your nurse this morning… Could you confirm your full name and date of birth… I'm just going to check your blood pressure now, if that's alright."

questions.stem: Which expression means "I will be responsible for your care today"?
options: I'll be looking after you today.
It's a pleasure to meet you.
questions.explanation: "I'm Dr / Nurse [name]. I'll be looking after you today." Observing is what a student does.

questions.stem: The written self-introduction (70–90 words) must include:
options: One sentence explaining what will happen during the visit
questions.explanation: Name, role, what will happen during the visit, and a polite closing question.

questions.stem: In the controlled speaking practice, students rewrite the model dialogue by changing:
options: The procedure mentioned at the end
questions.explanation: Rewrite it by changing the role and the procedure mentioned at the end.
